explanation: In 1926 customs officers taxed his polished bronze Bird in Space as a manufactured metal object. In 1928 a court ruled it was art, so no duty was owed.

claims.text: In Brancusi v. United States, decided in 1928, a US court ruled that Constantin Brâncuși's Bird in Space was a work of art.
In 1926 US customs officials refused to treat Bird in Space as art and charged duty on it as a manufactured object of metal.
The court's ruling meant the sculpture could enter the United States free of duty.
